Global growth is broadening, and business activity is picking up. The Chief Investment Office (CIO) believes 2026 will be shaped by supportive fiscal conditions, rising earnings and an accelerating AI‑industrial investment cycle. “Recently we’ve experienced above-average volatility across the markets,” says Chris Hyzy, Chief Investment Officer for Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank. “This volatility has pressured metals prices and high-growth mega-cap shares as well. In the context of all of this, we’re focusing on six key portfolio considerations we believe matter most this year.”

02:56 Idea 2 — Stay overweight equities, diversify globally
03:50 Idea 3 — Prepare for shifting sector leadership
05:05 Idea 4 — Use fixed income for ballast

08:25 Closing recap & final thoughts

#Portfolio #PortfolioStrategy

I have learned many lessons throughout the year, one of the biggest being that managing a sizable amount of capital means that trying to get those triple-digit returns are not going to be as easy. I also learned that when you are up +199% YTD (my portfolio on October 9th, and I imagine many others seeing an ATH during that time) then maybe taking some risk off the table and hedging wouldn’t be that bad of an idea. I am sure that my thoughts will change and adjust as the year progresses and there may be some names that I choose not to hold or trim or add to as we enter 2026, but I tried to lay out a framework for how I am thinking of managing capital and hopefully it serves as a useful tool for anyone else who is establishing a mental model of portfolio management.
